title: Lattice Scriber
pages: Craft with a Prism Core, an Infused Lattice Core, two sealed steel plates, a Gauge Block (top right), a Rotary Encoder (middle left), a Linear Encoder (bottom left), a hopper, a Ball Screw (bottom centre) and a Pneumatic Cylinder (middle right). The core comes from the Lattice Infuser and gates this t8 apparatus. Make the cylinder from four sealed plates, iron bars as a tube, a Pressure Gasket, sticky piston, glass air port and redstone control. It positions the light scribing head quickly; the ball screw still provides fine feed. Glass alone or the oil-filled Hydraulic Cylinder cannot substitute. Air pressure, stroke and compressor hookup are symbolic; this craft does not add a compressed-air network.

Gauge Block (RP-C09): polish one Tool Steel Stock in the formed tier-7 Prism Polisher for 220 ticks at 24 FE/t, with glowstone directly above and below the machine. This lapped reference sets a fixed length when aligning the tier-8 scriber feed; the encoders sense motion but cannot establish that reference alone. Feed stock through a top or horizontal port and extract below. A raw plate cannot replace the Gauge Block in the top-right controller slot. The NIST Gage Block Handbook describes length standards and their calibration; this game route abstracts lapping and does not certify a real tolerance or traceability (https://www.nist.gov/publications/gage-block-handbook).

Ball Screw: craft a Drive Shaft between two Tempered Steel nut halves, with a chromium ingot (forge:ingots/chromium, standing in for hardened chromium bearing-steel balls) above and below. Like a real ball screw, it turns rotation into a fine, repeatable linear feed, which the scriber needs to rule evenly spaced lines. Redstone alone no longer substitutes for the feed screw. Ball screws are stacked components; craft them by hand or with any crafting automation.

Rotary Encoder (middle left): flange one Stainless Vessel Stock into an Encoder Ring Blank in the Flange Press, then etch it in the Heliostat Etcher into a Graduated Encoder Ring. Craft an Optical Encoder Readhead from two sealed steel plates around a Signal Matrix (its signal processor), with a Ground Lens between two glowstone dust (the light source) below. Stack readhead, graduated ring and a Drive Shaft hub vertically to make the encoder. Mounted on the ball screw drive, it reports the screw's angle so the servo knows where the scribing head is; the screw alone only moves it. As with real ring encoders, the ruled resolution is not the same as installed accuracy, which also depends on mounting; this craft does not simulate either. Glass panes no longer substitute for the encoder. Encoders are stacked components; craft them by hand or with crafting automation.

Linear Encoder (bottom left): etch one Stainless Vessel Stock in the Heliostat Etcher into a straight Graduated Linear Scale (220 ticks, 20 FE/t). Mount it below a second Optical Encoder Readhead and above a Sealed Steel Plate. The readhead measures carriage travel directly along the scale, while the Rotary Encoder measures ball-screw angle; backlash can make these differ. A bare scale, unmarked stock or another rotary encoder cannot substitute. The etcher uses the same formed structure and hand-fed input as the ring route, so automate only the readhead and final craft with ordinary crafting equipment. This is a simplified optical scale: graduations are a game etching step, and resolution, thermal expansion and installed accuracy are not simulated.

Insert material from the top or horizontal faces; extract results below. Configure side modes in the GUI. Provide 22 FE/t or use the crank. A full output pauses work; stored items, FE and progress survive chunk reload.

Scribe a Sealed Steel Plate into a Scribed Plate, required in the Lattice Engraver craft. Nineteen datapack recipes cut distinct construction blocks into useful shapes. The scriber nests its cuts better than a hand stonecutter: 4 andesite, basalt, blackstone, diorite, granite, quartz block, red sandstone or stone become 5 polished or brick blocks, and 2 bricks, cobblestone, mossy cobblestone, mud bricks, nether bricks or purpur become 5 slabs. Deepslate, cobbled deepslate, end stone, prismarine and sandstone stay at the stonecutter yield because other machines would turn a batch bonus into a repeatable loop. Besides that, three tagged metal recipes turn 2 forge:ingots/thallium into 3 chains, 2 forge:ingots/vanadium into a grindstone and 3 forge:ingots/zirconium into a stonecutter. JEI lists input, output, duration, FE and priority.

Programmed Logic Controller (RP-C08): craft a Logic Board Blank from a comparator over a Signal Matrix (Signal Imprinter) over one Annealed Copper terminal strip, then scribe one blank for 200 ticks at 24 FE/t. Scribing cuts the ladder-logic trace pattern that turns the loose decision board into a sequencing controller; the Lattice Engraver needs it in its middle-right crafting slot to sequence its engraving passes. A glass pane or the unscribed blank is rejected. Hoppers can feed blanks from the top or sides and pull controllers from below. Scan time, I/O count and the program itself are abstracted; no real PLC firmware is modelled.
